title: The Lowest Common Ancestor in a Search Tree

concept.title: The order of the values tells you where the two nodes separate
body: In a binary search tree the common ancestor can be found **without searching both subtrees**. Start at the root. If both `p` and `q` are **smaller** than the node, they are both in the left subtree: go left. If both are **larger**, go right. In every other case (one is smaller and the other larger, or one equals the node) the roads to `p` and `q` split exactly here, so this node is the lowest common ancestor.
This takes one step per level, O(h), and needs no recursion. Compare it with the general tree version: there the values give no hint where the nodes are, so the whole tree may have to be searched.

statement: Given a binary search tree and two values `p` and `q` that are in the tree (they can be equal), print the value of their lowest common ancestor: the deepest node that has both of them in its subtree (a node is in its own subtree).
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
outputFormat: Print the value of the lowest common ancestor.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
The tree is a binary search tree (all values are different).
Both `p` and `q` are values of nodes of the tree.

examples.note: 2 is in the left subtree of 6 and 8 in the right one: the answer is 6.
4 is in the subtree of 2: the answer is 2.

hints: If p and q are both smaller than the node value, go left; if both are larger, go right.
Otherwise the current node is the answer.
A loop is enough; no recursion is needed.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root

    if root is None:

        return
    out = []

explanation: The walk goes left when both values are smaller and right when both are larger; the first node where they are not on the same side (or equal to it) is the lowest common ancestor.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def lca_bst(root, p, q):
    cur = root
    while cur is not None:
        if p < cur.val and q < cur.val:
            cur = cur.left
        elif p > cur.val and q > cur.val:
            cur = cur.right
        else:
            return cur
    return None

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()
p, q = map(int, input().split())

print(lca_bst(build_tree(vals), p, q).val)
